claim: Defines the binary cross-entropy loss supervising the CNN classification output chat, with target c in {0,1} where 1 means the image patch is centered on a ball.
Defines the Huber loss supervising the ball-diameter regression dhat: quadratic for |d-dhat| <= delta, linear beyond delta, with target diameter d in pixels.
Defines the training objective as an alpha-weighted combination of the diameter-regression Huber loss and the classification BCE loss; the diameter term is ignored for non-ball inputs.
Defines the 3x3 camera intrinsic matrix K parameterized by focal length f, pixel densities mu_x/mu_y, skew coefficient gamma, and principal point (u_x,u_y).
Gives the 3D rays of the ball center b^c and the two diametrically opposed ball edges e^c_{+/-} in camera coordinates, by inverting the intrinsic matrix K and rectifying image coordinates with R.

Gives the world-coordinate 3D ball position b^o from the true ball diameter phi, camera rotation R and center c^o: the center ray is scaled by the ratio of the true diameter to the vertical spread between the two edge rays.
Defines the second-degree (gravity-only) ball motion model F over time t from initial position p_0 and initial velocity dot{p}_0, with g = 9.81 m/s^2, ignoring friction, ball spin and other effects.
Fits the motion-model parameters by least squares: chooses the initial position and velocity minimizing the summed squared error between the model trajectory and the N annotated positions.
Selects the final ball detection candidate as the image patch I_j whose CNN classification score is highest among the k candidate patches.
